messages.subject: NIMBLE and external simulator
parts:
Hello!

I would like to ask if it is possible to configure NIMBLE such that we can call an external simulator within R (using the command system2()), which will return the value used to determine the acceptance of the proposed parameter set that will be used in the MCMC method. 

As a starting point, we have now set up some R code to call some external Java code (which we are using as an example for our simulator):


output <- system2("java", args = paste("bbox.Diplomat", runs, prob),

                 stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE, stdin = "", input = NULL,

                 env = character(), wait = TRUE, timeout = 0)


where the Java code "bbox.Diplomat" will provide the necessary return value.


If this is possible, we will then look into more details regarding the NIMBLE syntax to set up the procedure (e.g. NIMBLE code, MCMC object). I wonder if there is an option like the example in https://r-nimble.org/examples “Simulating from a model”, but where the data are generated by calling an external simulator.


Thank you in advance, any help will be very much appreciated.

Kind regards,

Ludovica Luisa Vissat

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: NIMBLE and external simulator
parts:
Hi Ludovica,

Thanks for your question.  I don't fully follow your use case, but let me try to address your question.

In model code, a node can be deterministic or stochastic.  A stochastic node has a distribution function (a "d" function in standard R distribution notation) and a simulation function (an "r" function in standard R notation).  For MCMC sampling, the "d" function is used to calculate log probabilities for stochastic nodes.  I'm confused because you are asking about calling a simulator (by which we would mean an "r" function) to determine acceptance in MCMC updates (which would typically use a "d" function).  You may be using terms differently.  Can you clarify your use case?   (There are methods, like Particle MCMC, where many simulations are used to obtain an unbiased estimate of an intractable likelihood and that estimate is used for MCMC updating, but that is somewhat specialized.  Please say if you are in any kind of use case like that.)

Either way, here is an outline of how you could connect either a "d" function or an "r" function to your external call.

1. Declare a model node to follow a stochastic declaration that you will define:

output[1:T] ~ dCustom( <parameters> )  ## Automatically calls dCustom for log probability and rCustom for stochastic simulation.

2. Write dCustom and, optionally, rCustom, as nimbleFunctions.  Please see our User Manual Chapter 12: https://r-nimble.org/html_manual/cha-user-defined.html

You only need to provide rCustom if your MCMC (or other method) will need stochastic simulations, which is not usually the case, with the possible exception of initialization if you are not providing inits (which, typically, you should).  You always need to provide dCustom.

3. To have either dCustom and/or rCustom call an R function, create a nimbleRcall for that purpose.  Please see our User Manual section 11.7: https://r-nimble.org/html_manual/cha-RCfunctions.html#sec:calling-R-code

An alternative, if you don't need much else in the model, would be to run the MCMC uncompiled, since the computational overhead might be in your external code anyway.  In that case, you could put the system2 call directly in the nimbleFunction for dCustom and/or rCustom, since they will simply execute in R.

If you need the external call for a deterministic calculation, you can do that in a similar way with a user-defined function rather than a user-defined distribution.

I hope that helps.  As you dig into these layers, let us know further questions.

-Perry
